name: Communications Management Plan
purpose: A component of the project management plan that describes how project communications will be planned, structured, implemented and monitored for effectiveness. It lists who needs which information, how it is delivered, how often and by whom, the assumptions and constraints on communication, and a glossary. It is updated periodically as stakeholders join and leave and communication needs change.

elements.guidance: The people or groups who need project information and their specific requirements.
The information to be communicated, including language, format, content and level of detail.
How it is delivered, for example email, meetings, web meetings.
How often the information is given and under what circumstances.
The name of the person or group that provides the information.
Assumptions about communication. The book gives one element row for assumptions and constraints; the blank form prints two columns.
Constraints, which can include proprietary, secure or sensitive information and the restrictions on distributing it.
Terms or acronyms unique to the project or used in a unique way.

tailoring: When several organizations work on the project, add the person responsible for authorizing release of internal or confidential information, and how different communication hardware, software and technologies will be handled so everyone is reached.
For a multinational team, account for the business language, the currency unit of measure, translation and other factors needed for effective communication across countries and cultures.
On a project with a large communication component, identify the resources, time and budget allocated to communication activities.
For complex communication needs, include a flowchart of the sequence of communication events.
